title: Unable to open BlueStacks 5 using CmdPal.
author: karedoea
summary: Command Palette discovers BlueStacks 5 but Windows returns access denied when launching the shortcut; direct shortcut behavior and sanitized .lnk properties are still needed.

status.detail: The bug report identifies the launch failure, but cross-launcher failure means the shortcut itself may be invalid or privileged.
status.label: Needs shortcut launch details

next_action.reason: This distinguishes a CmdPal launch-path defect from a shortcut or Windows-shell constraint.
next_action.label: Ask for direct shortcut behavior

evidence: CmdPal finds and displays BlueStacks 5.lnk, so discovery succeeds.
Downloaded CmdPal log records AppCommand.cs::StartExe failing for C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\BlueStacks 5.lnk with access denied.
The reporter says .lnk files with extra startup parameters cannot be opened in both CmdPal and Flow Launcher.
Current labels are Issue-Bug, Product-Command Palette, Needs-Triage, and Needs-Team-Response; there are no assignees or linked fixes.
Duplicate search for BlueStacks CmdPal returned only this issue.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask whether the exact Start Menu shortcut opens directly and request sanitized Target, Start in, arguments, and elevation settings.
judgment.rationale: The downloaded report confirms AppCommand.StartExe gets access denied for the BlueStacks Start Menu shortcut. The reporter also says parameterized shortcuts fail in Flow Launcher, so the current evidence does not prove CmdPal alone mishandles a valid shortcut.

issue_context.summary: Command Palette can discover the BlueStacks Start Menu shortcut, but pressing Enter produces no response. The uploaded bug report contains an access-denied launch error, while the reporter also observes similar failure in Flow Launcher for parameterized shortcuts.
known_information: PowerToys version is 0.101.2362.0 on Windows 11 Pro 25H2.
The reporter uploaded PowerToysReport.zip after a maintainer requested a bug report.
The diagnostic log shows access denied when CmdPal starts the BlueStacks shortcut from the Start Menu.
The reporter identified BlueStacks Pie x64 and said shortcuts with extra startup parameters also fail in Flow Launcher.

information_gaps.information: Whether the exact BlueStacks 5.lnk opens when double-clicked from the Start Menu folder or File Explorer.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Open C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs and double-click the same shortcut.
information_gaps.why_needed: Distinguishes a CmdPal-specific launch failure from a shortcut Windows itself cannot shell-open.

information_gaps.information: Sanitized Target, Start in, command-line arguments, and Run as administrator setting from the shortcut properties.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Open the shortcut Properties dialog and copy the values with personal paths or identifiers removed.
information_gaps.why_needed: Determines whether CmdPal must preserve special arguments, working directory, or elevation behavior.

inferences: The failure is after result discovery, in the launch path.
The common failure across launchers suggests the .lnk target, arguments, working directory, or elevation behavior may be the deciding factor.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue, all comments, labels, timeline, duplicate search results, and downloaded diagnostic ZIP.
Confirmed no linked issue, linked PR, assignee, or direct-shell-open result for the exact shortcut.
issue_context.analysis: The current diagnostic excerpt is useful and another generic archive is not the next step. Direct shell-open behavior and sanitized shortcut properties are the minimum facts needed to decide whether CmdPal should change shortcut launch handling.

actions.note: Draft only; no upstream comment is posted without explicit approval.

comment.body: Thanks for uploading the PowerToys bug report. It shows that Command Palette finds BlueStacks 5.lnk, then Windows returns access denied when CmdPal tries to launch that shortcut. You also noted that parameterized shortcuts fail in Flow Launcher, so the remaining question is whether CmdPal is mishandling a valid shortcut or whether this shortcut itself cannot be shell-opened. Please check whether C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\BlueStacks 5.lnk opens when double-clicked directly, and share the sanitized shortcut **Target**, **Start in**, command-line arguments, and whether **Run as administrator** is enabled. Those details will tell us whether the fix belongs in CmdPal's shortcut-launch path or in the shortcut/configuration. There is no need to upload another bug report unless the behavior changes.

actions.label: Ask how the shortcut launches directly
